PullRequest.Title: sessions: align experimental composer controls
PullRequest.Body: ## Summary - add keyboard commands for focusing the Agents Window workspace and harness pickers, including shortcut-aware hovers, context-menu keybinding configuration, and accessibility help - add an opt-in new-session footer that groups the folder, branch, New Worktree, and harness controls - align desktop running-session mode, approval, model, and context-usage controls with the experimental composer layout while preserving the existing phone layout - keep the context-usage control clear of editor text at rest and while expanded - preserve the existing layouts unless both the experimental composer layout and unified workspace picker settings are enabled ## Enablement The experimental layouts are enabled only when both of these application settings are `true`: - `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` (experimental, defaults to `false`) - `sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled` The picker focus commands, shortcut-aware hovers, context-menu keybinding configuration, and accessibility help require the unified workspace picker but do not require the experimental layout setting. ## Screenshots ### New session composer Fixes #337144 Fixes #337145 Fixes #337150

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and resize the experimental new-session composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous construction of the existing editor/toolbars, relocation of workspace/repository/session controls, and responsive picker measurement must complete before the composer is laid out. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation was added to this critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed number of composer controls and provider-contributed menu items; responsive work scales with the small toolbar DOM subtree, not transcript or workspace count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread layout path. Resize/mutation observers serialize layout and guard re-entry with _isLayouting.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration observables retain current values; no new cache, cache miss, negative-cache, or coalescing behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff widens responsive observation and performs DOM relocation, but traced mutations are bounded state transitions rather than per-keystroke rebuilding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout cost depends on enabled provider and voice controls, but cardinality is bounded and changes are tied to initial render, resize, or discrete toolbar mutations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added work is fixed-size UI layout work under an opt-in experiment and does not establish a hot or scaling performance mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch the experimental layout setting or cross the desktop/phone breakpoint in new and running sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The setting/context event synchronously toggles classes, relocates existing DOM nodes, updates toolbar visibility, and relayouts the input editor before the new layout is visible.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently instantiated session views and a fixed number of controls per view; the trigger is an infrequent setting or viewport-class transition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread updates per instantiated view; no asynchronous fan-out or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration values and context keys are read from existing in-memory services; no cold/warm cache difference.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous relayout path and its bounded trigger frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously instantiated views varies, but the Agents Window grid bounds practical view count and the triggering events are infrequent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the work is necessary for the explicit layout transition and is not on a frequent interaction path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the workspace or harness picker through the new keyboard commands
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Command routing finds the focused/active view and invokes the same existing showPicker path used by pointer and keyboard activation. Workspace items and harness types are built synchronously from existing provider/session state before the popup appears.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open a native folder-selection dialog only after the user chooses the existing Browse item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one dialog operation per explicit Browse selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Browse action and file-dialog boundary existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not on picker-open critical path; it blocks only the subsequent explicit Browse workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace picker construction scales with deduplicated recent workspaces and registered providers; harness picker construction scales with available provider session types. The diff does not increase either collection or rebuild frequency beyond a user command invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One picker-open operation per command; existing action-widget visibility guards prevent simultaneous duplicate picker presentation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing recent-workspace/provider state is reused; the new commands neither bypass nor add caching and do not change cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no new expensive boundary or additional per-item boundary call is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Recent workspace and provider counts vary, but the command is a new invocation route to an existing user-triggered path rather than automatic fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the shortcut exposes existing picker work without increasing its per-open cost or moving it onto an automatic hot path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update picker keybindings and context-menu presentation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each rendered workspace/harness trigger updates one delayed hover when keybindings or the unified-picker setting changes; context-menu actions are created only on explicit invocation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two picker triggers per new-session composer, multiplied by the bounded number of instantiated composers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event delivery; each trigger owns and replaces one disposable presentation store, with no parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Keybinding lookup uses the existing keybinding service; no changed cache lifecycle or miss behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that listeners are disposed by render/owner stores and retained state stays bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom keybinding updates are rare; exact number of live composers varies but remains bounded by visible views.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: fixed listener and hover-update cost with correct cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh agent-host repository controls when experiment settings, providers, viewport, or visible sessions change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution synchronously rebuilds menu registrations from visible sessions and in-memory session schemas; this must finish before toolbar menu updates reflect the new ordering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible session slots times renderable schema properties after filtering; no per-property IPC, filesystem, network, or subprocess calls occur.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized synchronous menu rebuilds; no Promise fan-out or concurrent boundary operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider session configs are read from existing in-memory provider state; property command registrations are retained and reused by command id.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the loop cardinality and absence of transitive expensive boundaries on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider schema sizes vary, but expected properties and visible view count are small, and new refresh triggers are infrequent configuration changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added configuration-triggered refresh is infrequent, bounded, and required to change ordering.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 25 changed files and relevant call paths. Checked synchronous render/layout work, responsive observer scope, DOM relocation, menu rebuilds, picker invocation boundaries, keybinding listeners, cleanup ownership, cache behavior, and concurrency. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.
